title: Jacob Misiorowski adds to Cy Young Award resume with historic start
content:
Jacob Misiorowski’s 20th start of the season began in an all-too-familiar place, a swinging strikeout on a pitch clocked at 103.4 mph. Then it continued, one after another, the Milwaukee Brewers’ young ace having struck out eight of the first nine batters he faced, his levers long and his velocity as high as it’s ever been.

Such was the predicament the lowly Colorado Rockies found themselves in on Sunday at American Family Field. The National League’s frontrunner for the Cy Young Award continued his historic 2026 campaign by, well, making more history.

As chronicled by MLB.com’s Sarah Langs, Misiorowski’s three strikeouts at 104 mph or swifter were the most by a pitcher in a game in the pitch tracking era (since 2008). Those three Ks topped the two that Misiorowski set a month ago on June 12.

They came on pitches that clocked in at:

• 104.3 mph (swinging strikeout against Hunter Goodman in the top of the first inning)
• 104.5 mph (called strikeout against Kyle Karros in the top of the second)
• 104.1 mph (swinging strikeout against Cole Carrigg in the top of the second)

It didn’t end there, either.

His eight strikeouts on pitches clocked at 103 mph or faster were the most by any pitcher since 2008, topping a record that Misiorowski has matched and reset four times this season.

*Since 2008

Misiorowski also became the first pitcher since 1920 with 11 or more strikeouts and no hits allowed through four innings. At 24 years old and 114 days, Misiorowski also became the youngest starter in 50 seasons to strike out 11 batters through his first four innings pitched.

In all, 66 of his 83 pitches were fastballs. None of those 66 pitches clocked under 100 mph, another record for the most 100 mph or faster pitches in a single game since 2008.

Even his lone blemish, a fifth-inning solo homer allowed to Carrigg on a 101.9 mph fastball that was outside the strike zone, was historic. It was the fastest pitch a Rockie has homered against since 2008, and tied for the 12th-fastest that anyone has ever clubbed for a longball in that same span.

Misiorowski’s final line: 5 innings, 1 hit, 1 run, zero walks, 12 strikeouts.

His 1.58 ERA leads all pitchers, NL or AL, while his 185 strikeouts are 18 more than the next closest starter (Dylan Cease, 167). His 0.75 WHIP is 15 points lower than the next qualified starter (Yoshinobu Yamamoto, 0.90), and his .149 batting average against leads all pitchers.

A bout of arm fatigue saw the right-hander scratched from his final start of the first half and later limited to just four innings in his first start coming out of the All-Star break. Six days later, it was all merely a blip on what has otherwise been a pitching season for the ages.
